objective: An audit of Relay found two independent latent defects in its usage modules, each in a small pure module whose own comments say what it intends and whose code does something else. Fix both, in place, without changing anything else. (A) `deriveUsageThresholdEvents` in `src/relay/usage/usage-thresholds.ts`: the file header says the latch remembers which thresholds already notified, that the same key never notifies twice, and that only dropping back below a threshold (or entering a new reset window) re-arms it. A refresh in which a section's reading is unknown (null) currently drops that section's keys from the latch, so the next ordinary refresh with the same reading and the same reset window notifies the same crossing again. (B) `projectUsageBar` in `src/relay/usage/usage-projection.ts`: `tone` is documented as the highest warning level currently visible in the snapshot, but when none of the figures the summary shows is known the function returns early with a hard-coded `idle`, even when the weekly window is known and fully used. `seed/src/relay/usage-fixes.test.ts` is already written and currently fails; it pins the main behaviours of each fix. The two modules do not depend on one another, so the fixes are independent. The files to edit exist and are tracked by git: edit them in place.
requirements: A. In `deriveUsageThresholdEvents`, a section whose reading is unknown (`percentUsed` null for the five-hour or weekly window, `remaining` null for Mission Contracts) neither notifies nor changes that section's part of the latch: the keys the previous latch held for that section are carried into the new latch exactly as they were. A key belongs to a section by its leading segment (`five_hour`, `weekly`, `mission_contracts`), and only that section's keys are carried. When every section is unknown and the previous latch is empty, there are no events and the very same latch object is returned.

A. A KNOWN reading behaves exactly as before: a key whose threshold is no longer reached is removed, a new reset window or provenance (which changes the key) starts clean, and a newly reached threshold notifies once with the most severe newly crossed threshold of the section. Event text, kinds, ordering and the returned-latch-identity rule (the same latch object when nothing changed, which includes the case where every key of the previous latch was carried over because its section is unknown) do not change.

B. In `projectUsageBar`, `tone` reflects the most severe of the five-hour window, the weekly window and the Mission Contract count whenever any of them is known, including in the state where nothing the summary shows is known. The summary text (`USAGE · UNAVAILABLE` or `USAGE · UPDATING`) and the aria label in that state do not change, and the simulated-snapshot path (tone `demo`) and the ordinary path do not change.
No function outside these two fixes changes behaviour.
constraints: Edit `src/relay/usage/usage-thresholds.ts` and `src/relay/usage/usage-projection.ts` in place. `src/relay/usage/usage-contracts.ts` is part of the workspace because `usage-thresholds.ts` imports it; it is read-only. You have `Read`, `Glob`, `Grep` and `Edit`; you cannot create files or run commands, and you do not need to.
Do not edit `src/relay/usage-fixes.test.ts`. It is the specification you are implementing against, not part of the deliverable.
Use only what the files already import plus Node built-ins. Add no dependency and no import from outside this workspace: the sandbox that runs the test has no network access and no `node_modules`.
Do not change any exported name, signature or type, and do not mutate the inputs of the functions you change.
Do not reformat code you are not changing and do not make unrelated cleanups, however tempting; a change that is not one of the two fixes is out of scope. Do not touch `.julius/`.

acceptanceCriteria.text: An unknown reading never changes its section's part of the latch, in any of the three sections, and never produces an event; only a known reading below a threshold, or a new reset window, re-arms it.
Known readings behave exactly as before: removal below a threshold, one event for the most severe newly crossed threshold, unchanged text and ordering, and the same latch object when nothing changed.

The usage bar's tone is the most severe of the three known figures in every non-simulated state, including the state whose summary is UNAVAILABLE or UPDATING; the summary and aria text of that state are unchanged.
Only `usage-thresholds.ts` and `usage-projection.ts` are changed, using no new dependency; neither mutates its inputs.
